en: The Apadāna of the Elder Soṇakoṭivīsa Avaṭaphalavagga 9 The Apadāna of the Elder Soṇakoṭivīsa I gave a soṇa-fruit to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was seated beneath a tree. By that root of merit, I have attained the fruit of stream-entry. Having abandoned the five lower fetters, I am one who will not return to this world again. I shall attain parinibbāna in the interval; this is my final birth. Thus did I speak. This is the true Dhamma. May there be well-being. May all beings be happy. May all beings be free from suffering. “In the dispensation of Vipassin,
I have made a single shelter for the Saṅgha of the four quarters.”
In the royal capital of Bandhumatī,
having spread my skin over the ground for a shelter, I renounced it.
With an uplifted mind and joyful heart,
I then made this aspiration:
"May I please the Perfectly Enlightened One."
May I receive the going-forth;
may I touch the unsurpassed Nibbāna,
the supreme peace.
By that very root of merit,
I wandered for ninety eons,
having been both a deva and a human.
Having performed merit, I shone forth.
Then, by the remainder of that karma,
in this final existence:
In Campā, I was born as the only son of the chief merchant.
As soon as I was born, having heard...
This was my father’s wish:
"I shall give no fewer than twenty koṭis to the prince."
And my body hairs on both soles of my feet have grown four finger-breadths long;
they are fine and soft to the touch.
As beautiful as cotton or silk;
ninety-one aeons have passed,
and this one more besides.
I do not recall ever placing my foot upon the bare ground;
thus have I propitiated the Perfectly Enlightened One.
I went forth into homelessness;
I have attained arahantship,
become cooled, and am extinguished.
The All-Seeing One has declared me the foremost among those who have aroused energy:
"I am an Arhat whose taints are destroyed."
Possessing the six supernormal knowledges and great psychic power,
I gave that gift back in the ninety-first aeon.
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving a shelter.
The defilements have been burnt away by me.
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
... [and so on] ... the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) have been attained.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus spoke the elder Soṇa Koṭivīsa.
In the presence of the community of monks,
when questioned, he gave an answer at the great lake Anotatta.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Soṇa Koṭivīsa speak these verses.
This is the ninth legend of the elder Soṇa Koṭivīsa.
